course_name_original: Simulación, Control e Instrumentación de Procesos Químicos
course_name_en: Simulation, Control and Instrumentation of Chemical Processes
prerequisites: Métodos numéricos (numerical resolution of differential equations)
Automatización y Control (control system tuning techniques)

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the particularities of modeling, simulation, control, and instrumentation of chemical processes.
Utilize basic chemical engineering principles to model and simulate the dynamic and static behavior of chemical processes.
Formulate, design, and correctly specify advanced control strategies and optimization of chemical processes, as well as simulate their dynamic behavior.
Know and select the necessary instruments (sensors, transmitters, and actuators) to implement chemical process control and optimization techniques.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Simulation of controlled Chemical Processes
Simulation and control of complete plants
Basic elements of the control loop
assessment_rules: For ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade is calculated as (0.8 x G + 0.2 x TG) if the global exam is passed. To pass the subject, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be obtained in this formula. If the minimums are not reached, the grade will be the minimum between the obtained formula score and 4.0. The global exam requires at least 4 out of 10 points and consists of a theoretical/practical part and a problem-solving part, each contributing 50% to the exam grade; at least 30% of the assigned score must be obtained in each part. For differentiated evaluation, group tutorials (TG) are replaced by a project (E), with the formula being (0.8 x G + 0.2 x E).
